title: Many and One — the reading copy (EA-MANY-AND-ONE-COMPLETE v2.5.1, the machine)
creator: Lee Sharks
description: The reading copy of *Many and One* — the research machine from which the journal article was cut. Ten sections that descend from the theorems to their applications: I Division of God (Metaphysics Λ 9 against Prior Analytics I.31), II Division of Life (De anima 413b, seal and wax), III Many Accounts (Sophist 232a), IV Collection (Phaedrus 249c / De memoria 453a), V Divided Person (Republic 395b / Symposium 223d), VI Many Voices (one maker, λόγος-level identity), VII The Machine (the six-transmission-function apparatus, the paper's one positive measurement), VIII Insufficiency of ὕλη (every lexical instrument reported failing where 1075a1 predicts), IX Order of the Corpus (genre and form, not chronology), X The Flood (the corpus as a solution to transmission). The apparatus is seated at each section's head; pass standings, retractions, nulls and audit passes are intact in the end-matter. §§I–IV owe nothing to the authorship question; the seam is declared at the head of §V. Version 2.5.1 of 2026-08-31: citation pass (Greek loci verified against canonical texts, nine emendations), incorporation pass (~30 insertions from the notebook reread, every retraction traveling with its material), and five internal contradictions repaired. Held from publication by the author's own ruling while the article was under editorial consideration at Ancient Philosophy; released on the editor's decline of 2026-09-02. The four registers of 2026-08-31 (renumbering-and-seating ledger, citation pass, notebook reread, incorporation) are attached. The article cut from this copy, the notebook, the measurement register, the frozen pre-registration ledger, and the technical report are separate deposits.

wiki_article: Many and One — the reading copy (EA-MANY-AND-ONE-COMPLETE v2.5.1) is the research machine of Lee Sharks's investigation into whether the received two-author partition of the Platonic and Aristotelian corpora is established by the texts, or whether the texts offer one maker as a reading. Ten sections descend from theorems to applications. §I reads Metaphysics Λ 9 against Prior Analytics I.31: division, which I.31 files as a small part of the method (μικρόν τι μόριον τῆς εἰρημένης μεθόδου) and diagnoses as begging its question because it takes the universal as middle, terminates in Λ 9 where the terms divided are not other; §II reads De anima 413b's seal-and-wax as one in actuality, many in potentiality; §III the Sophist's six accounts of one kind; §IV collection ἐκ πολλῶν εἰς ἕν through Phaedrus 249c and De memoria 453a; §V the divided person at Republic 395b and Symposium 223d, with the seam declared at its head; §VI the two demonstrations and the λόγος-level identity of the maker; §VII The Machine, the six-transmission-function apparatus that is the paper's one positive measurement (procedural habits shared by the two corpora at high rates and not transmitting in a documented master–student control); §VIII the insufficiency of ὕλη, fifteen lexical instruments each killed by its control, with the object-conditioning result — Aristotle's within-domain dispersion 0.0571 against Plato's total 0.0570, the residual ordered by object-space — presented as §II's formula at corpus scale; §IX the order of the corpus by genre and form rather than chronology; §X the flood, the corpus as a solution to transmission. The apparatus is seated at each section's head; retractions, nulls and the standings of five passes are in the end-matter. The copy was held from publication by the author's ruling while the article cut from it was under consideration at Ancient Philosophy, and released on the editor's decline. It is the maximal surface of the line that runs from Socrates as Orthonym through the notebook (#1569), the measurement register (#1570), the pre-registration ledger (#1571), the technical report (#1572), and the reception measurement The Particle (#1574).

defines_concepts.definition: The result that a corpus's within-domain stylistic dispersion equals or exceeds the other corpus's total dispersion, so that the residual variance is ordered by object-space rather than by maker; Aristotle 0.0571 within-domain against Plato 0.0570 total.
The declared point in the paper (head of §V) at which the theorems of §§I–IV, which owe nothing to the authorship question, are first applied to it.
The criterion for one-not-two makers: neither position could have made the object alone; the object exists only at the join; a person so constituted is exactly as long as the chain of passing links.
